findings.text: The auto-generated `__rich_repr__` calls `getattr(self, param.name)` for every `__init__` parameter. If a class stores a parameter under a different name (for example `def __init__(self, x): self._x = x`), this raises `AttributeError`, which is re-raised as `ReprError`. As a result `repr(obj)` itself throws instead of returning a string. Because `@rich_repr` is now an alias for `auto`, existing decorated classes are affected too.

The `hasattr(cls, "__rich_repr__")` check also matches an inherited `__rich_repr__`. For `@auto(angular=True) class Sub(Base)` where `Base` already has `__rich_repr__`, the `angular` flag is silently ignored. Subclasses of an auto-decorated class also reuse the parent's `angular` setting.

0.reason: The generated `__rich_repr__` is meant to read each `__init__` parameter back as an attribute of the same name. Classes already decorated with `@rich_repr` also define their own `__rich_repr__`, so line 119's `hasattr` check skips generation and they are not affected as the finding claims.

1.reason: Line 119 only sets `angular` when no `__rich_repr__` exists, including an inherited one. So `@auto(angular=True)` on a class that defines or inherits `__rich_repr__` silently drops the flag, and the parent's function-level `angular` attribute is used instead.
